description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.scope: Phase 5 hardening backend (harden-phase5-api): isolated e2e stack tooling and coverage tests
args.focus: Check against openspec/changes/harden-phase5-api (spec delta specs/platform-foundation/spec.md and design.md). Pay attention to: any way tools/e2e-stack.mjs or compose.e2e.yaml could address the owner's Compose project 'doucko' or its volumes (doucko_doucko-pgdata, doucko_doucko-storage) — project name from env, COMPOSE_* variables, relative -f paths, down -v scope; values from .env or the process environment leaking into the e2e stack; ports published on anything but 127.0.0.1 or services other than the frontend (NFR-2); the seed not being idempotent (duplicates on re-run, races, matching by excerpt), sending workbook content or PII (NFR-3, NFR-4); the generated PDF being invalid; secrets or real values committed in tools/e2e-stack.env; the new tests asserting real behaviour rather than padding coverage; Windows path handling.

findings.title: Seed adopts any mission at topic+position 1 without checking or fixing its taskIds, so re-runs can fail or report tasks the mission doesn't contain
findings.evidence: `mission = missions.find((m) => m.topicId === SEED_MISSION.topicId && m.position === SEED_MISSION.position)` matches on position only. If the mission at that position has other tasks (an e2e test edited it, or something created position 1 first) or has no tasks (a DRAFT with 0 tasks; publishing needs at least 1, CA-D7), the seed still returns the freshly collected `taskIds` as if they were in the mission, or the publish PUT fails with 400. The spec scenario says a re-run leaves "the same three published tasks and one published mission", but nothing checks that the mission actually holds those tasks.
findings.suggestion: After finding the mission, compare `mission.taskIds` with the seed `taskIds`. If they differ, PUT /api/admin/missions/{id} with the seed list (or fail loudly) before publishing, and return `mission.taskIds`.

findings.title: Design names a scratch/qa-lock mutex for up..down that does not exist
findings.evidence: Risks & mitigations says "Two agents starting the stack at once → the shared `scratch/qa-lock` mkdir lock covers `up`..`down`." No file in the repo except design.md mentions `qa-lock`, and tools/e2e-stack.mjs runs `up`/`down -v` with no lock. With a fixed project name, one agent's `down -v` deletes the volumes of another agent's running suite. tasks.md marks everything [x], so the mitigation is claimed but missing.
findings.suggestion: Add a lock (mkdir of scratch/qa-lock, held from up through down) to tools/e2e-stack.mjs, or remove the claim from design.md and record the risk as accepted.

findings.title: Pre-up NFR-2 check accepts RFC 1918 addresses, but the spec requires the e2e frontend on 127.0.0.1 only
findings.evidence: `portProblems()` reuses `bindAddressProblem(port.host_ip || "0.0.0.0")`, which also accepts 10/8, 172.16/12 and 192.168/16 (the owner-stack rule). The spec delta says the stack publishes "only the frontend on `127.0.0.1:18082`". If the override drifts (for example, Compose ignores or mishandles `!override` and the base `${DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS}:8081` survives), a LAN or second port would pass the check. The check also never verifies the port is 18082.
findings.suggestion: For the e2e tool, require exactly one published port: service `frontend`, `host_ip === "127.0.0.1"`, `published == 18082`. Refuse anything else.

findings.title: Seed tooling (blankPdf, idempotent matching, AdminClient) has no automated test
findings.evidence: design.md says the pure parts in `tools/lib/e2e-stack.mjs` and `tools/lib/e2e-seed.mjs` are tested by E2eStackToolTest, but the test only runs `--dry-run` argv, the guard, a text regex over compose.e2e.yaml and the env file. Nothing checks that `blankPdf(2)` gives a parseable 2-page PDF (correct xref offsets; PDFBox page count) or that `seed` is idempotent against a fake client. The idempotency scenario in the spec delta has no executable mechanism apart from the manual proof in task 1.5.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that loads blankPdf(n) with PDFBox (already used by the backend for page counts) and asserts n pages. Add a node-level test that runs `seed` twice against an in-memory fake AdminClient and asserts no second create and identical results.

findings.title: composeEnv stripping is untested; the dry-run test only proves the -p argument
findings.evidence: The test sets `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=doucko` and checks the printed argv, but `-p` wins over that variable anyway. The real leak risk is the process environment overriding `--env-file` values: the owner's ADMIN_PASSWORD, DOUCKO_DB_PASSWORD, or the real DOUCKO_CHILD_DISPLAY_NAME (NFR-3) ending up in the e2e DB. That is handled only by `composeEnv`, which no test exercises. The dry-run output never includes the environment.
findings.suggestion: Make `--dry-run` also print the sorted keys of the stripped env, or unit-test `composeEnv` through `node -e`. Assert that DOUCKO_CHILD_DISPLAY_NAME, ADMIN_PASSWORD, DOUCKO_DB_PASSWORD, DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS and COMPOSE_* are absent.

findings.title: Env stripping is case-sensitive on a copied object; Windows env names are case-insensitive
findings.evidence: `const out = { ...env }` turns Windows' case-insensitive `process.env` into a plain case-sensitive object, and `delete out["DOUCKO_CHILD_DISPLAY_NAME"]` misses a key stored as, for example, `Doucko_Child_Display_Name`. Compose (Go) on Windows looks up environment variables case-insensitively, so such a variable would still override the committed e2e value.
findings.suggestion: Delete keys by case-insensitive comparison: `for (const k of Object.keys(out)) if (STRIP.includes(k.toUpperCase())) delete out[k]`.

findings.title: Task matching scans every seed task without stopping and ignores duplicates
findings.evidence: For each of the 3 definitions, the loop fetches every task whose `promptExcerpt.startsWith("E2E Seed")` and keeps the last match: `if (full.prompt === def.prompt) task = full;`. There is no `break`, so it makes N GETs per definition. If an earlier interrupted or concurrent run created duplicates, the seed quietly picks one and the spec's 'exactly one' state is never restored or reported.
findings.suggestion: Fetch the seed-prefixed tasks once into a map from prompt to tasks. If a prompt has more than one task, fail loudly (or warn) instead of choosing one.

findings.title: New TaskRules test repeats an existing page-range assertion
findings.evidence: `errors(draft(page = In.Ok(121))) shouldContainExactly listOf("sourceRef.page" to "page-range")` repeats the case at line 117 (`In.Ok(121)` in `page must lie within the source's page count`). The other three assertions in the new test cover real new branches (not-uuid, required + page-whole, source-unknown + page-whole); this line adds nothing.
findings.suggestion: Drop the last assertion, or replace it with a branch that is not covered yet.

findings.title: Design promises a qa-lock around up..seed..down that is not implemented; concurrent seeds create duplicates
findings.evidence: design.md:31 says "Two agents starting the stack at once → the shared scratch/qa-lock mkdir lock covers up..down", but grep finds no 'qa-lock' anywhere in tools/ or scripts/. The seed works by checking first and creating second (GET /api/admin/sources → find by title → POST). If two agents (or a Playwright globalSetup plus a manual run) seed at the same moment, both see the source as missing and both POST it, which gives two 'E2E Seed Source' rows and duplicate tasks. That breaks the spec scenario 'exactly one seed source'. Two parallel `down -v` / `up` calls can also wipe the stack while the other agent's suite is still running. Impact stays inside doucko-e2e. No owner data is at risk.
findings.suggestion: Take the mkdir lock (or an equivalent lock) in tools/e2e-stack.mjs for up/seed/down, as design.md describes, or remove the claim from design.md and state that runs must be serialised. Optionally make the seed fail loudly when it finds more than one match, so it never silently picks one.

findings.title: Seed treats any mission at topic+position 1 as the seed mission and never checks its task list
findings.evidence: `missions.find(m => m.topicId === SEED_MISSION.topicId && m.position === SEED_MISSION.position)` accepts any mission in that slot. If an e2e test, or an earlier partial seed, created a mission at Přirozená čísla/1 with other or no tasks, the seed logs 'exists' and publishes it. It then returns `taskIds` (the seed tasks) next to a `missionId` that does not contain them. Suites that rely on the returned plan would run against the wrong tasks. The same lenient matching applies to tasks: a match in any status (e.g. ARCHIVED) goes straight to PUT PUBLISHED, which may be refused and abort the seed.
findings.suggestion: Compare the found mission's task ids with the seed tasks. Refuse with a clear message if they differ, or update the mission. Handle non-DRAFT/non-PUBLISHED task states explicitly.

findings.title: Env-stripping guard (composeEnv) is not covered by any test; the 'environment names doucko' test only checks the static argv
findings.evidence: `--dry-run` prints `dockerArgsFor(command)`, which never reads the environment. So the test that sets COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=doucko would pass even if composeEnv() were deleted. Isolation actually holds because `-p` on the CLI beats the env var. But the other half of the design, keeping exported real values (ADMIN_PASSWORD, DOUCKO_DB_PASSWORD, DOUCKO_CHILD_DISPLAY_NAME, DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS from an owner shell that sourced .env) from overriding --env-file, has no regression test. If that list regresses, the owner's real child name and admin password would quietly flow into the e2e stack (NFR-3). The runtime NFR-2 check `portProblems()` is not tested either; the NFR-2 test only greps the YAML text.
findings.suggestion: Make --dry-run also print the keys of the environment the child process would get (or export composeEnv and test it via `node -e`). Assert that DOUCKO_CHILD_DISPLAY_NAME/ADMIN_PASSWORD/DOUCKO_DB_PASSWORD/DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS/COMPOSE_* set in the parent are absent and DOUCKO_FRONTEND_DIR is absolute. Add a test for the portProblems rule (non-frontend published port → refused), using a JSON fixture of `compose config` output.

findings.title: tasks.md marks review-gate and archive as done before this review and without evidence
findings.evidence: Items 4.3 ('review-gate; findings dispositioned in review-findings.json') and 4.5 ('Archive') are checked [x]. But openspec/changes/harden-phase5-api/ contains no review-findings.json, the change is still unarchived, and this review is the gate. findings.evidence: tasks.md:2.2 '[x] `node scripts/check-coverage-ratchet.mjs --update`'. proposal.md says 'Behavioural tests that restore line/branch coverage to at least the committed baseline; baseline ratcheted up'. quality/coverage-baseline.json was last changed in 1db68a2 (slice 9) and still reads statements 97.76 / branches 90.94. findings.title: Seed idempotency scenario has no automated test and no committed proof (task 1.5 ticked without evidence)
findings.evidence: Scenario: 'GIVEN a running e2e stack that was seeded once WHEN seed runs again THEN the admin API lists exactly one seed source, the same three published tasks and one published mission'. E2eStackToolTest only covers argv, env and the override text; seed()/blankPdf() are never called. tasks.md 1.5 '[x] Proof: up, seed twice, curl through 127.0.0.1:18082, down; `doucko` untouched' has no artifact: docs/qa/evidence ends at slice9-compose-smoke.md, with no phase-5 e2e proof.
findings.suggestion: Add a Node-level test of seed() against a fake AdminClient (in-memory sources/tasks/missions) that runs it twice and asserts one source, the same 3 task ids and 1 mission, all PUBLISHED. Also check blankPdf() with PDFBox from the Kotlin test (page count = 2). Commit docs/qa/evidence/phase5-e2e-stack-smoke.md with the real up/seed×2/down transcript, including `docker volume ls` showing doucko_doucko-pgdata unchanged.

findings.title: The mission is matched by topic+position only, so a foreign mission at position 1 counts as the seed mission
findings.evidence: `missions.find((m) => m.topicId === SEED_MISSION.topicId && m.position === SEED_MISSION.position)`. If a mission already sits at Přirozená čísla/1 (e.g. one the Playwright suite created on the same stack), the seed logs 'exists', may publish it, and returns its missionId with seed taskIds it doesn't contain. Mission membership is never compared with taskIds. The scenario wants 'the same … one published mission' built from the seed tasks.
findings.suggestion: After matching, check that mission.taskIds equal the seed taskIds and fail loudly if they don't, or pick a dedicated position nobody else uses. Write the chosen rule into design.md decision 4.

findings.title: Design promises a qa-lock for concurrent up..down/seed, but nothing implements it (concurrent seeds would duplicate)
findings.evidence: design.md Risks: 'Two agents starting the stack at once → the shared `scratch/qa-lock` mkdir lock covers `up`..`down`.' Grepping tools/ and scripts/ for 'qa-lock' finds nothing, and e2e-stack.mjs takes no lock. seed() is check-then-create (GET sources/tasks, then POST), so two concurrent seeds both create the source and tasks, which breaks 'exactly one seed source'.
findings.suggestion: Take the mkdir lock in e2e-stack.mjs around up/seed/down, or drop the claim from design.md and record the race as an accepted risk.

findings.title: Case-variant environment variables survive composeEnv on Windows
findings.evidence: `const out = { ...env }; … delete out[key]` deletes only the exact upper-case keys. On Windows, process.env is case-insensitive, but the spread copy is a plain object. Docker (Go, Windows) reads env case-insensitively, so e.g. `Admin_Password` or `doucko_db_password` from the user's environment would survive and override tools/e2e-stack.env. The project itself is safe because `-p doucko-e2e` wins over COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME.
findings.suggestion: Delete keys by case-insensitive comparison (`Object.keys(out).filter(k => BLOCKED.includes(k.toUpperCase()))`), and add a dry-run test that also prints the scrubbed env key set.

findings.title: The dry-run scenario never checks the child environment, so the env scrubbing (and the never-.env rule) is untested
findings.evidence: The requirement says configuration comes 'only from committed, clearly fake test values and never from `.env`'. design.md decision 2 says COMPOSE_* and the secret variables are removed from the child environment. The dry-run JSON (tools/e2e-stack.mjs:66) prints only docker argv, frontendDir and baseUrl, so no test can see that composeEnv removed ADMIN_PASSWORD, DOUCKO_DB_PASSWORD, COMPOSE_FILE and the rest. The test name says 'even when the environment names doucko', but it only proves `-p` precedence.
findings.suggestion: Add the scrubbed env keys (or a list of removed keys) to the dry-run output and assert that ADMIN_PASSWORD, DOUCKO_DB_PASSWORD and COMPOSE_FILE set in the test env are absent.

findings.title: The NFR-2 port check accepts any private LAN address, not only 127.0.0.1:18082
findings.evidence: The spec says 'publishing only the frontend on `127.0.0.1:18082`'. portProblems() reuses bindAddressProblem() from the real stack, which (per compose.yaml comments) allows RFC 1918 addresses, and it never checks the port number. The override hardcodes 127.0.0.1:18082 today, so this is only a weaker guard than the spec states.
findings.suggestion: In portProblems(), require host_ip === '127.0.0.1' and published == 18082 for the e2e project.

findings.title: The frontendDir test fails when the developer's own DOUCKO_FRONTEND_DIR is set; tests also carry NFR-3 traces that don't fit
findings.evidence: `dryRun("up")["frontendDir"] shouldBe File(root.parentFile, "frontend").path`. ProcessBuilder inherits the parent environment, so a DOUCKO_FRONTEND_DIR exported for a frontend worktree (the documented use) makes the default case fail. Also, `the frontend build context follows DOUCKO_FRONTEND_DIR` and `unknown commands and options are refused` are traced `// @trace NFR-3` (PII), which they don't verify.
findings.suggestion: Call builder.environment().remove("DOUCKO_FRONTEND_DIR") for the default case. Retrace those tests to the platform-foundation requirement, or drop the NFR-3 trace.

findings.title: Scope drift: `ps` command and DOUCKO_FRONTEND_DIR are not in the spec requirement
findings.evidence: The requirement names only `node tools/e2e-stack.mjs up|down|seed`. The code adds `ps` (COMMANDS = ["up","down","seed","ps"]) and a configurable frontend build context via DOUCKO_FRONTEND_DIR (compose.e2e.yaml:8). Both are mentioned only in proposal.md. The proposal also promises `npm e2e-stack:*`, but there is no `e2e-stack:ps` script.
findings.suggestion: Amend the spec delta to list `ps` and the DOUCKO_FRONTEND_DIR build context, or remove them.

findings.title: The generated blank PDF pages have no /Resources entry
findings.evidence: `<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 595 842] >>`. PDF 1.4 says /Resources is required (inheritable), and neither the Page nor the Pages node has one. Offsets and xref are correct (ASCII only, 20-byte entries). Lenient parsers like PDFBox accept the file, but the OpenAPI source upload contract (openapi.yaml ~l.373) returns 400 for 'unreadable page tree', so a stricter parser could reject the seed.
findings.suggestion: Add `/Resources << >>` to the Pages node, and test blankPdf(2) with the backend's own page counter.

result.reasoning: The mechanism is real. In tools/lib/e2e-seed.mjs:160-177, the seed picks the mission by topicId plus position and never reads or compares the mission's task list. When a mission already exists, the seed only publishes it if it isn't published yet, then returns the `taskIds` it gathered from the seed tasks, not the mission's actual tasks. Nothing else guards this. The caller (tools/e2e-stack.mjs seed) prints whatever comes back, and there's no reconciliation step anywhere. The Flyway migrations don't insert any missions, so on a fresh stack the seed creates the mission correctly. The bug shows up when the seed runs again on a stack that persists ('seed' is a separate command from 'up'/'down', and the file header promises idempotent re-runs). If an e2e test or a manual admin edit has changed or created the mission at grade-6 topic position 1 in the meantime, the seed reports that it adopted the mission even though the returned taskIds don't match what's in it. A draft with no tasks would make the publish PUT fail. So the claim that nothing checks the mission's contents is correct. I'm downgrading the severity: this is test tooling on a throwaway Compose project (doucko-e2e, and 'down' deletes the volumes). The bad state only happens if something other than the seed has changed missions on a reused stack. It's a test-reliability problem, not a product correctness problem.

The code does what the finding says. At tools/lib/e2e-seed.mjs:161 the seed picks the mission by `topicId` and `position === 1` only. It never compares `mission.taskIds` with the seed `taskIds`, and line 177 returns the freshly collected `taskIds` even when it reused an existing mission. V3__missions.sql has a `UNIQUE (topic_id, position)` constraint, so whichever mission holds position 1 in topic 6a00…0001 is the one the seed adopts. No migration seeds a mission there, and nothing else in the seed guards against this.

The damage is small and hard to trigger, though:
1. **Isolated test tooling only.** This is `tools/e2e-stack.mjs seed`, which runs against the throwaway `doucko-e2e` Compose project and its throwaway volumes. It isn't on any child or admin request path, so no real user or attacker can reach it.
2. **The seed's own re-runs are consistent.** On a fresh stack the seed creates the mission with exactly its three `taskIds`, so a second run adopts the right mission. The only way to get a mismatch is for something else to change topic+position 1 between runs: an e2e test that edits or recreates that mission, or a manual admin edit. I couldn't read `../frontend/e2e` (permission denied), so I can't confirm that any real-stack test actually does this.
3. **One failure mode is loud, not silent.** A DRAFT mission with 0 tasks makes the publish PUT return 400, and `AdminClient.request` throws, so `seed` exits 1 with a clear message. Only the "mission has different tasks" case is silent: the returned taskIds would be wrong and the spec's "same three published tasks and one published mission" would not hold.

Conclusion: the idempotency gap is real, but it only appears after an outside change on a test-only stack. Not refuted, but it should be downgraded from major to minor.

Confirmed: tools/e2e-stack.mjs takes no lock. `up` and `down` (lines 58-71) call docker directly, and the project name is fixed at `doucko-e2e`. So the tool itself does nothing to stop two runs at once. Within this repo, design.md:31 is the only place that mentions `qa-lock`.

The finding's evidence does not show that the mitigation is missing, though. design.md calls it "the **shared** `scratch/qa-lock`". In this repo, `scratch/` always means the machine-local `../scratch` folder that sits outside the repos and is shared by agents. Examples: docs/qa/evidence/slice8-red-run.md:33 and slice9-red-run.md:23 ("../scratch/… machine-local, not committed"), plus the archived proposals that point to `../scratch/slice9-backend-behaviour.md`. So the line describes a workflow convention that agents follow around the whole up..seed..suite..down run. It does not claim the tool implements a lock. Searching this repo for `qa-lock` can't prove that convention is absent. It would live in ../docs/factory or the agents' session protocol, and I was not allowed to read either, so I can't confirm the lock is missing. Note also that `up`, `seed` and `down` are separate processes by design. A lock that covers the whole run has to be held by the caller, so its absence from e2e-stack.mjs is expected, not a defect.

The risk that remains is real but minor. Nothing in the code enforces the convention, and two agents can share the same `doucko-e2e` stack, so one agent's `down -v` can wipe the stack another is using. This is a throwaway, loopback-only test stack, not product code, and it never touches the `doucko` project (`assertE2eProject`). "Major" with "high" confidence is too strong.

Refuted as stated ("the mitigation is claimed but missing"), because I could not confirm it. A fair minor follow-up would be to make design.md say the lock is a caller-held convention, or to have the tool check for it.

Confirmed inside this repo. Line 31 of design.md is the only place in the worktree that mentions `qa-lock`. Searching for "lock" or "scratch" under tools/ returns nothing. tools/e2e-stack.mjs runs `docker compose -p doucko-e2e up/down` with no locking at all. The project name is a hard-coded constant, so if two agents run on the same machine (worktrees are already used here), one agent's `down -v` would remove the containers and volumes another agent's suite is using. Nothing in the code prevents that.

Two caveats limit this. First, the word "shared" hints that the lock may be a workspace-level convention kept outside this repo, for example in ../docs/factory or the frontend's Playwright runner. I could not search those directories because access was denied, so I can't rule that out. Also, `up` and `down` run as separate processes, so a lock covering up..down would have to be held by the caller anyway, not inside e2e-stack.mjs. Second, the impact is limited to developer test tooling. The data is throwaway (fake values in a loopback-only stack), the owner's `doucko` project is guarded by `assertE2eProject`, and no real user or attacker can trigger it. The worst outcome is a flaky or broken e2e run.

So the finding stands as a gap between what the doc claims and what the code does (the mitigation is claimed and the tasks are marked done, but this repo doesn't implement it). It is not a major correctness defect. I recommend downgrading it to minor or doc-accuracy.

I couldn't find a way for the failure the finding describes to actually happen. Line 50 does call `bindAddressProblem`, which accepts private LAN (RFC 1918) addresses. But the finding's own example, where `!override` fails and the base `${DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS}:8081` port survives, can't lead to a LAN binding:

1. `composeEnv()` (`tools/lib/e2e-stack.mjs:48-63`) deletes `DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS` from the environment passed to docker compose. That covers both `config` and `up`, since both use the same `env`.
2. The only env file the e2e tool passes is `tools/e2e-stack.env`, and it sets only `DOUCKO_DB_PASSWORD`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `DOUCKO_CHILD_DISPLAY_NAME`. It never sets `DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS`.
3. So the base port can only render as `127.0.0.1:8081` (the default in `compose.yaml:68`). That is loopback, never a LAN address.

Line 52 also already refuses any published port on a service other than `frontend`, so a backend or db port can't slip through. A LAN address on the frontend could only appear if someone edited the committed `compose.e2e.yaml` (`ports: !override ["127.0.0.1:18082:80"]`). That is a reviewed code change, not a runtime path a check would need to catch.

What remains true is that the check doesn't pin the port to exactly `127.0.0.1:18082` and doesn't allow only one published port. That would be a reasonable extra safeguard, but it doesn't make the current code wrong: no reachable input leads to a non-loopback binding or a violation of the loopback requirement (NFR-2).

The scenario the finding describes can't happen with the committed code. The check is looser than the spec, but nothing a user or attacker controls can produce a LAN binding for it to miss.

1) The fallback scenario stays on loopback. The base `compose.yaml:68` publishes `"${DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS:-127.0.0.1}:8081:80"`. `composeEnv()` (tools/lib/e2e-stack.mjs:50-61) deletes `DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS` from the process environment.
